The prevalence of atrial fibrillation per 1,000 inhabitants varies significantly across Denmark's five administrative regions, with a clear and persistent divide between the highest and lowest burden areas over a five-year period from 2020/2021 to 2024/2025 [^src1]. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] consistently records the highest prevalence, acting as the leader in atrial fibrillation burden, reaching 27.1 per 1,000 inhabitants by 2024/2025 [^src1]. In contrast, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] remains the trailer, maintaining the lowest prevalence throughout the entire period and ending at 20.2 per 1,000 inhabitants in 2024/2025 [^src1]. This gap of nearly 7 cases per 1,000 inhabitants between the highest and lowest regions in the final year highlights a substantial geographic disparity in the condition's distribution [^src1].

Examining the trends across the five years, most regions experienced an overall increase in prevalence, though the trajectories differ [^src1]. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] showed a steady upward trend, climbing from 26.0 in 2020/2021 to 27.1 in 2024/2025 [^src1]. [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] also saw overall increases, with Syddanmark rising from 24.6 to 25.3 before plateauing at 25.3 in the final two years, and Nordjylland moving from 24.6 to 25.2 despite a slight dip to 24.4 in 2022/2023 [^src1]. [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] experienced minor fluctuations, dipping to 21.8 in 2022/2023, but ultimately grew from 21.8 in 2020/2021 to 22.4 in 2024/2025 [^src1]. [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] was the only region to see a decline in the middle years, dropping from 20.3 to 19.8 in 2022/2023 and 2023/2024, before rebounding to 20.2 in the final year [^src1].

An outlier in this dataset is [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], which is the only region to consistently remain below the 21.0 threshold, while all other regions stayed at or above 21.8 throughout the entire five-year span [^src1]. Furthermore, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] started at the exact same prevalence of 24.6 in 2020/2021 but diverged slightly in subsequent years, with Nordjylland showing more year-to-year volatility compared to the steady climb and plateau of Syddanmark [^src1].
